newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary cen.bank to set benchmark yield-traders.
newsitem.headline: Hungary cen.bank to set benchmark yield-traders.

text.p: The one-year bonds to be issued by the National Bank of Hungary (NBH) on Friday are unlikely to have an immediate impact on the government securities market, but will serve with important benchmark yields in the longer term, traders said on Wednesday.
"(The issue) is unlikely to have any direct impact (on government securities yields)," said Laszlo Lakatos of Bank Austria Investment.
"It is very likely that the NBH will offer the bonds at the same yield level as the twelve month depo (20.25 percent)."

The NBH said Tuesday evening that for the first time it would begin issuing bonds on the domestic market from June 20, adding that the yields to be offered on the bonds will give indications for the markets on the yield levels which the central bank regarded as appropriate.
Traders said the bonds should replace the NBH's 12-month deposit facility, which was introduced three months ago, but remained illiquid.
"The market expects the 12-month facility to be replaced and practically that is what will change," said Lakatos.
Gabor Szogi of Creditanstalt Securities added that the NBH may also abolish the six-month deposit facility after beginning the issue of the bonds.
Traders said the one-year bonds would provide the NBH with a flexible tool for intervening on the government securities market.
"With the bonds the NBH can intervene on the markets in a direct and rapid way," Lakatos said, adding that the NBh was unlikely to change the yield on the bonds often.

The yield on the one-year NBH bond will serve as a support for 12-month discount Treasury bill yields, and indirectly they will influence the yields of both discount Treasury bills with shorter maturities and of government bonds, traders said.
